## Task
Do A and B name the same business concept (the same real-world thing, so the classes model one concept under different names)? Concepts that merely share attributes such as an id or a date are not the same.

### A
concept: Booking
where: SessionService (uses), src/business/sessionService.ts, component business
code:
=====SOURCE-BEGIN
const ticketsUsed = active.reduce((n, b) => n + b.tickets, 0);
=====SOURCE-END=====

### B
concept: Club Booking
where: ClubBookingRepository (uses), src/persistence/clubBookingRepository.ts, component persistence
code:
=====SOURCE-BEGIN
private readonly bookings = new Map<string, ClubBooking>();
=====SOURCE-END=====
graph:
- class ClubBookingRepository (node 440da90bcde7901a): layer infrastructure, component persistence, fan-out 0, fan-in 7
- <- CALLS Method ClubBookingService.create
- <- CALLS Method ClubBookingService.get
- <- CALLS Method ClubBookingService.invoice
- <- CALLS Method ClubBookingService.list
- <- CALLS Method SessionService.effectiveCapacity
- <- CONSTRUCTOR_INJECTS Class ClubBookingService
- <- CONSTRUCTOR_INJECTS Class SessionService

response.rationale: Booking is a per-session ticket booking: SessionService sums `b.tickets` over active bookings fetched with BookingRepository.findBySession. Club Booking is a separate entity (`Map<string, ClubBooking>`) in its own ClubBookingRepository. It has its own ClubBookingService (create/get/list/invoice) and is looked up by date (findByDate), not by session. SessionService uses the two through separate repositories, and only reads club bookings to adjust effectiveCapacity. Separate storage, a different lookup key and invoicing that only club bookings have point to related but different concepts (individual ticket bookings vs. club/group bookings), not one concept under two names.
